newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks seen vulnerable, to test support.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks seen vulnerable, to test support.

text.p: Singapore stocks were seen in a mixed mood on Thursday and vulnerable to technical pressures after sliding below 2,000 points on Wednesday.
Dealers said institutions and retail investors alike were unwilling to hold length due to the bearish outlook.
"People are selling into spurts. The verdict is that this is a box and we won't grow out of this for the next two quarters," a dealer with a foreign institution said.
On Wednesday, the Straits Times Industrial Index (STII) eased 19.12 points to 1,985.14 on a thin volume of 95 million shares. Over-the-counter stocks fared slightly better.

Dealers expect smaller issues to be in favour again, while blue chips continue to lag and the index to search for a bottom. A retracement in the Dow Jones on Wednesday would also cast a bearish cloud on sentiment, dealers said.
